claims.text: With cache-aside the application, not the cache, loads data: it asks the cache first and, on a miss, reads the data store and puts the result in the cache itself.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Azure Architecture Center: Cache-Aside pattern; glossary entry cache-aside

claims.text: ProductsController.Get(int id) calls products.FindAsync(id) on its IProductRepository and answers NotFound() for null, otherwise Ok(new ProductDto(...)); List() reads DonHangDbContext (db.Products) directly.

AddDonHangInfrastructure registers IProductRepository as scoped: a new ProductCache built around the registered EfProductRepository, the IConnectionMultiplexer and an ILogger<ProductCache>; the controller only sees IProductRepository.

ProductCache.FindAsync builds key product:{id}, calls GetAsync; a non-null result is returned (hit); otherwise, after the per-key lock and a second GetAsync, it calls inner.FindAsync and SetAsync only when the product is not null.

On a hit, GetAsync turns the stored text into a Product with JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Product>(..., JsonSerializerOptions.Web); no EF Core query runs. The stored JSON is {"id":3,"name":"Tai nghe","priceVnd":890000}.
SetAsync serializes the product to JSON and calls StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl) with Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), which stores the string under the key with a 5-minute expiry.
claims.source_hint: ProductCache.cs:18, 78-89; StackExchange.Redis API: IDatabaseAsync.StringSetAsync(key, value, expiry)

claims.text: EfProductRepository.FindAsync calls db.Products.FindAsync(id); with the request's new scoped DbContext this sends one query to PostgreSQL.
claims.source_hint: EfProductRepository.cs:9 @ stage-2; EF Core docs: DbSet.FindAsync (tracked entity first, else database query)

claims.text: GetAsync and SetAsync catch exceptions that are RedisException or RedisTimeoutException, log a warning, and continue: GetAsync returns null (treated as a miss), SetAsync lets the request go on.
With the redis container stopped, GET product:3 fails with RedisConnectionException (a subclass of RedisException), so the catch applies and the request is answered from PostgreSQL.
claims.source_hint: api log at stage-2 after cache-aside.sh (RedisConnectionException ... GET product:3); StackExchange.Redis API: RedisConnectionException : RedisException

claims.text: A ConnectionMultiplexer is designed to be shared and reused between callers, and should not be created per operation; it is thread-safe.
claims.source_hint: StackExchange.Redis docs: Basic Usage ('designed to be shared and reused between callers')

claims.text: services.AddSingleton<IConnectionMultiplexer>(...) creates one ConnectionMultiplexer via ConfigurationOptions.Parse(redisConfiguration), BacklogPolicy = BacklogPolicy.FailFast, ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect(options).
abortConnect=false lets Connect return a multiplexer even while Redis is down, and the multiplexer keeps trying to connect in the background.
claims.source_hint: StackExchange.Redis docs: Configuration (abortConnect; reconnects in background); ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:29-32

claims.text: BacklogPolicy.FailFast makes each Redis command fail at once while there is no connection, instead of waiting in a backlog for the connection to come back.

cache-aside.sh output: after DEL, the first GET /api/v1/products/3 is 200 with 1 products query and product:3 then holds the JSON; the repeat is 200 with 0 queries; with redis stopped it is 200 with 1 query.
cache-aside.sh runs on the host; it counts lines containing 'FROM products' in docker compose logs of api before and after each request, and stops then restarts the redis service.
EF Core logs each SQL command it sends under category Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command at Information level, which the lab's api service enables.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Simple logging / event ids (CommandExecuted); docker-compose.yml:124-127 @ stage-2

claims.text: While redis is stopped, one product request logs the warning 'Redis read of product:3 failed; reading PostgreSQL instead' twice, because FindAsync calls GetAsync twice on a miss.
claims.source_hint: ProductCache.cs:73 @ stage-2; docker compose logs api after cache-aside.sh (checked 2026-09-28)

claims.text: docker compose logs api prints the log output of the api service's container, run from the folder holding docker-compose.yml.
On a miss ProductCache does Redis GETs (GetAsync twice: before and after the per-key lock), then the query, then a Redis write, so a miss costs more than a read with no cache.
A cache pays off when the same data is read far more often than it changes; each cached copy is one more place that can hold an old value.
claims.source_hint: Azure Architecture Center: Cache-Aside pattern, 'When to use this pattern' / consistency considerations

claims.text: For a product that does not exist, inner.FindAsync returns null, SetAsync is not called (nothing is written to Redis for that id), and the controller answers 404.
StackExchange.Redis is the Redis client library DonHang.Api uses (DonHang.Infrastructure package reference).
Until product:3 expires (5 minutes after it was written), requests for product 3 are hits unless the key is deleted first (UpdatePriceAsync deletes it after a price change) or a Redis error occurs.

The helpers at the top of cache-aside.sh: redis runs redis-cli in the redis container via docker compose exec; get_product_3 curls GET /api/v1/products/3, prints body and status code, then the products query count.
